sections.title: Convenience Retail Digital Commerce (7-Eleven)
sections.description: 7-Eleven (Irving TX HQ) — the world's largest convenience store chain with 13,000+ US stores and a rapidly growing digital commerce platform.

blocks.heading: 7NOW delivery demand prediction
paragraphs: ML for 7-Eleven's delivery service demand — predicting which convenience products will be ordered through 7NOW at the store level, time of day, and location for the impulse purchase and delivery dynamics of convenience delivery.

blocks.heading: 7-Eleven app loyalty personalization
paragraphs: ML for 7-Eleven's loyalty program and digital offers — personalized promotional offers for the 7Rewards members based on purchase history, location, and time of day purchase patterns.

blocks.heading: Store-level inventory for digital orders
paragraphs: ML for managing in-store inventory to support digital order fulfillment — predicting which items are most likely to be ordered digitally and ensuring those items are in stock at 7-Eleven stores serving high-delivery-demand areas.

sections.title: Luxury eCommerce Personalization (Neiman Marcus)
sections.description: Neiman Marcus (Dallas HQ) — the US's most significant luxury department store retailer with a growing luxury eCommerce platform.

blocks.heading: Luxury product recommendation
paragraphs: ML for Neiman Marcus's luxury eCommerce personalization — high-consideration purchase recommendation that accounts for the long decision cycles, brand affinity, and style evolution patterns of Neiman Marcus's high-income customer base. Luxury recommendation differs fundamentally from mass market recommendation: a Neiman Marcus customer browsing a $4,000 Valentino dress requires very different recommendation logic than an Amazon customer browsing $30 shoes.

blocks.heading: Customer lifetime value prediction
paragraphs: ML for predicting CLV for Neiman Marcus's top tier customers — the InCircle Loyalty program's highest tiers represent customers worth tens of thousands annually in revenue, and retention ML for this segment has enormous commercial impact.

blocks.heading: Personal stylist augmentation
paragraphs: ML supporting Neiman Marcus's personal styling programs — providing data-driven insights to human stylists about customer preferences, purchase timing, and size/style evolution.

sections.title: Fashion and Apparel eCommerce (Fossil Group)
sections.description: Fossil Group (Richardson TX HQ) — global fashion accessories company operating Fossil, Skagen, and licensed Michael Kors, Kate Spade, and Armani watches.

blocks.heading: Watch and accessories demand forecasting
paragraphs: ML for Fossil's complex seasonal demand — fashion accessories demand is driven by trend cycles, color palettes, and seasonal collections that require ML models incorporating fashion trend signals beyond historical sales.

blocks.heading: DTC channel personalization
paragraphs: Recommendation and personalization ML for Fossil's growing direct-to-consumer digital channels — competing with Amazon and department store digital for the customer's fashion accessories purchase.

sections.title: Dallas's eCommerce AI advantages
sections.description: Dallas has structural advantages for eCommerce AI that its consumer market size alone doesn't capture.

blocks.heading: Central US last-mile advantage
paragraphs: DFW's central US geography creates a logistics advantage for eCommerce that has attracted major fulfillment centers from Amazon, Walmart, and Target. AI that optimizes last-mile delivery from DFW's fulfillment network can simultaneously improve delivery times and reduce shipping cost in ways that East or West Coast-centric fulfillment cannot replicate.

blocks.heading: Texas Privacy Protection Act's eCommerce implications
paragraphs: Texas's consumer privacy law affects the consumer data practices of eCommerce companies with large Texas customer bases — and Dallas's position as a Texas commercial hub means that Texas TPPA compliance is a design requirement for most consumer-facing Dallas eCommerce AI applications.

blocks.heading: DFW's bilingual eCommerce market
paragraphs: Dallas's large and growing Hispanic population — including a significant Spanish-speaking consumer base — creates eCommerce AI demand for Spanish-English bilingual experiences. AI-powered search, recommendation, and customer service in Spanish is increasingly a competitive necessity for Dallas-market eCommerce rather than a premium feature.
